core_job: "Get it sorted": a renter or homeowner with a specific job (a leak, a lock-out, a cracked phone screen, alterations, a car service, a tutor) starts a job. NearServe builds a call list of real local businesses in that trade from OpenStreetMap (Overpass, around a typed town or postcode). The user calls each one from the app and logs what was said. They compare the quotes, mark one hired with the date they agreed, and close the job with the price paid and a private "would use again" note. The user can also add someone who isn't on OpenStreetMap. NearServe never contacts a business itself, and everything stays on the device. This replaces today's fake "Book a slot" calendar: it made up 60-minute slots that no business ever receives, and the booking marked itself "Completed" and could then be reviewed.
signature: The call-around board, a customer-side call sheet and quote board for one job. (a) Call-now ordering: businesses open now (from their published OSM opening_hours, with a time-zone guard based on longitude) come first, then those with no published hours, then closed ones marked "Opens Tue 08:00", and finally those with no phone, which get "Find their number in Maps". (b) A return-from-call logger: when the user comes back from a tel: call, NearServe asks how it went (no answer, left a message, call back at a time, quote with amount/basis/earliest start, can't do it, visit agreed). A "Log a call" button covers iPads and calls made from another phone. (c) Like-for-like comparison: fixed prices are grouped and compared only with fixed prices, hourly rates only with hourly rates, and "needs a visit to quote" is never ranked against a number. Each listing shows how fresh it is, taken from OSM meta timestamp and check_date; in a London sample of 300 listings, 32% had not been edited in more than 3 years. Gap against the competitors I checked, from App Store descriptions read through the iTunes API: Thumbtack, Angi and Taskrabbit only compare quotes from their own members, and Angi for Pros describes the paid-lead model; quote trackers such as QuoteIQ, Joist and QuotePulse are for contractors, not customers. How these apps behave beyond their descriptions is not verified.

Delete the NEARSERVE_API_BASE_URL/TOKEN defines and HttpDirectorySource, NoDirectorySource, sample_notice (Sampleton) and every isSample branch, the estimator, the slot generator and the booking, review and saved models and screens, and the rating, price, verified and lead-time fields and filters. Pass when: grep for fromEnvironment finds only AglAdIds in main.dart; grep for the banned strings finds 0; strings on the release App.framework finds 0.

M2 Directory scoped to NearServe (overlap G11). Three category groups: Home repairs, Fix it, Lessons/pets/more. Drop health (doctors, dentists, clinics, physio), fitness and massage. Add the measured trade and repair tags: hvac, locksmith/key_cutter, roofer, painter, carpenter, glaziery, gardener, electronics_repair, shoe_repair, tailor, bicycle repair. Switch the query to out center tags meta and keep only timestamp and check_date. Replace the dead fallback overpass.private.coffee (HTTP 000 twice) with maps.mail.ru (HTTP 200). Rows show only facts: distance, open state, phone glyph, freshness chip, your history. Never 'Contact the provider for pricing' or 'Availability not published'. Show an honest count line, plus an 'Add one you know' prompt when there are fewer than 5 results.

M3 Core job: Jobs end to end. Pure-Dart model: Job, Candidate (with a snapshot), CallRecord, Verdict. Status rules are enforced in a repository and nothing advances by itself. Versioned shared_preferences store, with migration of old saved ids and bookings. Screens: new job, job page, outcome sheet, hire sheet, close sheet, add-someone-not-listed. Wording is honest ('You noted', 'Hired by you'); no 'booking', 'confirmed' or 'review'. A journey widget test runs Austin fixture → leaking tap → 3 plumbers → log 3 calls → hire → done → restart → 'You hired them · would use again'.

M4 Signature: call-around board. Pure functions rankForCalling (with the time-zone guard) and quote grouping with 'lowest' per basis. A pendingCall is persisted before tel:, and the outcome sheet opens on resume. When canLaunchUrl is false the app shows Copy and Log a call. Every candidate has the freshness line, 'Find their number in Maps' and a 'Fix this listing on OpenStreetMap' browser link. Unit and widget tests; no price is ever rendered that the user did not enter.

M5 Depth. Directory with search, Open now / Has phone / Updated in 3 years filters, Your pros and a full listing page. Job history with search and a status filter. Copy and Email job summary with no new native plugin (Podfile.lock carries someone else's edits). Offline: jobs render from snapshots, and the last call list per area and category is cached with its fetch time. App-specific empty, busy (504 is common, measured 3 times today), offline and error states, each tested.

M6 Own identity. Home is a Jobs board with no NavigationBar. One AglAdBanner, in directory results only, and no tab interstitial. Two-step onboarding ('Where do you need help?' and 'How NearServe works', button 'Start a job'). Palette 'Work-order pad': ink navy #1C2B4A primary, duplicate-sheet pink #FBE3DF, stamp green #2E7D4F, danger #9E2F2A, desk #EEF0F3, plus a dark set; hand-built ColorScheme with a contrast test. Fonts: Work Sans for UI and Space Mono for numbers, phones and dates, bundled, with google_fonts and Inter removed (no other app or spec uses either font). Shape: 4px ticket cards with a perforated tear line, a rubber-stamp HIRED/DONE label and CustomPainter category icons instead of emoji. New hand-built icon (remove generate_app_icons.py:74). New LaunchScreen on #1C2B4A, so the shasum is no longer 3f6a9b27…. Cupertino icons and transitions on iOS.

M7 Proven. flutter analyze clean and all tests pass (baseline today: analyze clean, +410 passing). New tests cover M2–M6 and an extended release_sanity grep. Ten booking/estimate/http/saved test files are removed only together with their code and named in the commit; the other screen tests are rewritten, none skipped. Launch on the simulator and look at the screenshots. Commit only the paths changed, never fastlane/, Podfile.lock or project.pbxproj, and push to main.
